=== FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m3 ===
- scripts/review_claude_fixer_nonblocking.py:demote_with_diagnostics, lines ~319-325 | severity=NIT | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: Each reviewer's `review_<slug>.txt` is opened and read three times per demote call, once for outputs, once for `reviewer_bound_rejections`, and once for the legacy `reviewer_rejections` count.
  WHY: With the six-reviewer roster this is six extra file reads on top of the two already needed; it does not change behaviour but inflates IO on every Claude-fixer hand-off.
- scripts/review_claude_fixer_nonblocking.py:main(), the CLAUDE_FIXER_NONBLOCKING log line ~ line 494 | severity=NIT | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: `successful_reviewers(args.reviews_dir)` is called a second time after `demote_with_diagnostics` already populated the same map, re-scanning `status_review_*.txt` purely to compute `len()` for the log line.
  WHY: Redundant directory walk and six re-reads of `status_review_*.txt` on every CLI invocation; behaviour is correct, only the cost is wasteful.
- scripts/review_claude_fixer_nonblocking.py:reviewer_bound_rejections (around the REJECTED_FINDING_ID_RE / REJECTED_FINDING_RE pair)
  Issue: A REJECTED_FINDING line with no id but with the legacy proximity match still goes through the reviewer_rejections fallback used for the legacy count. Today the fallback path is read-only (it counts and ignores), but the function itself never validates the rest of the line beyond a regex match; a malformed rest that happens to match REJECTED_FINDING_RE could underreport ambiguity for the LEGACY_REJECTIONS diagnostic.
  Suggested minimal fix: Drop the legacy reviewer_rejections call in main entirely once enough runner versions guarantee ids; alternatively have the helper return only the count it can prove against the file, so the LEGACY_REJECTIONS line cannot silently include unparsable rejections.
  Estimated lines changed: 3
